title: Free-floating Subdivisions: Classes of Persons
summary: List of topical (sec. F) and form (sec. G) subdivisions that may be used on a free-floating basis under headings for classes of persons: age and sex groups, social/economic/political categories, afflicted persons, members of religions, employees and occupational groups, classes of persons formed with place or corporate subdivisions (e.g. Stanford University--Faculty), and classes qualified by ethnic/national adjectives. Not for social classes, ethnic groups/nationalities (H 1103), or religious orders (H 1186). The full list with May Subd Geog flags and usage notes is in rules/lists/H1100.json. LC no longer assigns form subdivisions (LCGFT/LCDGT instead).
validation_rules: The subdivisions on the sec. F (topical) and sec. G (form) lists may be used as free-floating subdivisions under headings for classes of persons: age and sex groups; social, economic, and political categories; types of afflicted persons; members of religions; employees and occupational groups (e.g. `Youth`, `Women`, `Fathers`, `Poor`, `Political prisoners`, `People with mental disabilities`, `Liver--Cancer--Patients`, `Hare Krishnas`, `Judges`, `Darts players`, `High technology industries--Employees`). (H 1100 sec. C)

Classes of persons formed with subdivisions under places or corporate bodies are covered, e.g. `Great Britain--Officials and employees`, `Stanford University--Faculty`, `United States. Navy--Officers`. (H 1100 sec. C)
Classes of persons qualified by ethnic or national adjectives are covered by this list (not H 1103), e.g. `African American dentists`, `French students`, `Foreign workers, Turkish`. (H 1100 sec. C)
The list may be used under groups of literary authors unless it conflicts with a subdivision designated for literary authors in H 1155.2. (H 1100 sec. C)
Do not apply this list to social classes or collective social groupings (e.g. `Nobility`, `Working class`, `Families`, `Clans`). (H 1100 sec. D)
Do not apply this list to ethnic groups and nationalities (e.g. `Hispanic Americans`, `Māori (New Zealand people)`, `French`); use H 1103. (H 1100 sec. D)
Do not apply this list to members of religious and monastic orders; use H 1186. (H 1100 sec. D)

When a free-floating subdivision conflicts with an established heading, use the established heading, e.g. `Child abuse`, not `Children--Abuse of`; but headings of the type `Teachers, Training of` were changed to `Teachers--Training of`. (H 1100 sec. E)
A subdivision may be followed by a geographic subdivision only if it is marked "Yes" (May Subd Geog) on the list (`may_subd_geog` in rules/lists/H1100.json). (H 1100 secs. F-G)

Cross-reference entries on the list (May Subd Geog column `--`, e.g. `Appointment, qualifications, tenure, etc.`, `Costume`, `Hygiene`, `Treatment`, `Working conditions`) are not valid subdivisions; use the referenced subdivision (e.g. `--Selection and appointment`, `--Clothing`, `--Health and hygiene`, `--Care`, `--Employment`). (H 1100 sec. F)

Do not use `--Hospitals`, `--Mortality`, or `--Surgery` under headings for persons with specific diseases; use `[disease]--Hospitals`, `[disease]--Mortality`, `[disease]--Surgery` (cf. H 1150). (H 1100 sec. F)
Do not use `--Psychology` under classes of afflicted persons if the heading for the disease or affliction exists; use `[disease or affliction]--Psychological aspects`. (H 1100 sec. F)
Do not use `--Political activity` under headings for people chiefly known for political involvement (e.g. `Politicians`, `Political candidates`, `Presidents`). (H 1100 sec. F)

Do not use `--Societies, etc.` under a class of persons if the heading for the discipline can be assigned: `Engineering--Societies, etc.`, not `Engineers--Societies, etc.`; but `Women engineers--Societies, etc.` and `African American engineers--Societies, etc.` are valid. (H 1100 sec. F)

Use `--Examinations`, `--Vocational guidance`, and `--Handbooks, manuals, etc.` only if a heading for the corresponding field or activity does not exist or cannot be established, e.g. `Hospital ward clerks--Examinations`, `Allied health personnel--Vocational guidance`, `Nurses' aides--Handbooks, manuals, etc.` (H 1100 secs. F-G)

Many subdivisions are restricted to occupational groups and types of employees (e.g. `--Bonding`, `--Certification`, `--Dismissal of`, `--In-service training`, `--Job satisfaction`, `--Labor unions`, `--Licenses`, `--Recruiting`, `--Selection and appointment`, `--Training of`, `--Workload`); `--Fees` is for professional groups; `--Salaries, etc.` for classes of professional or public employees. (H 1100 sec. F)
Wages of nonprofessional employees are expressed as `Wages--[industry or class of wage earners]`, not `--Salaries, etc.` (H 1100 sec. F, Salaries, etc.)

Century subdivisions `--16th century` through `--21st century` are free-floating only after `--Economic conditions`, `--History`, `--Intellectual life`, `--Social conditions`, and `--Social life and customs` under classes of persons. (H 1100 sec. F)

Some form subdivisions are valid only as combinations with a topical element: `--Archives--Microform catalogs`, `--Biography--Sources`, `--Examinations--Study guides`, `--History--Sources`, `--Social conditions--Humor`, `--Social life and customs--Humor` (first element coded $x, last $v). (H 1100 sec. G)
`--Job descriptions` ($v) may be subdivided geographically and is used only under occupational groups and types of employees. (H 1100 sec. G)

[LC practice] LC catalogers no longer use form subdivisions; assign LCGFT (e.g. `Textbooks`) and, for demographic groups, LCDGT (e.g. `German speakers`, `Arabic, Students of`). Form subdivisions remain valid LCSH. (H 1100 secs. A, G)

sections.heading: A. Background
sections.text: LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Textbooks*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.

sections.heading: B. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-01: Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: C. Types of headings covered
sections.text:
The subdivisions listed in sec. E and sec. F, below, may be used on a free-floating basis, as appropriate, under subject headings for classes of persons, including age and sex groups; social, economic, and political categories of persons; types of afflicted persons; members of religions; employees and occupational groups; etc.

Examples:

```
Youth
Women
Fathers
Poor
Political prisoners
People with mental disabilities
Liver--Cancer--Patients
Hare Krishnas
Judges
Darts players
High technology industries--Employees
```

The category includes headings for classes of persons that are formulated with subdivisions used under names of places or individual corporate bodies.

Examples:

```
Great Britain--Officials and employees
Stanford University--Faculty
United States. Navy--Officers
```

Headings for classes of persons qualified by ethnic or national adjectival qualifiers are also included in this category.

Examples:

```
African American dentists
French students
Foreign workers, Turkish
```

Subdivisions from this list may be used under headings for groups of literary authors where there is no conflict with a subdivision specifically designated for use under literary authors in H 1155.2.

sections.heading: D. Types of headings not covered
sections.text:
This instruction sheet does not apply to headings for social classes or collective social groupings.

Examples of excluded headings:

```
Nobility
Working class
Families
Clans
```

The instruction sheet also does not apply to headings for ethnic groups and nationalities.

Examples of excluded headings:

```
Hispanic Americans
Māori (New Zealand people)
French
```

For subdivisions used under ethnic groups and nationalities, see H 1103.

This instruction sheet also does not apply to headings for members of religious and monastic orders. For subdivisions used under names of individual religious and monastic orders, see H 1186.

sections.heading: E. Conflicts
sections.text: Determine if the use of a free-floating subdivision from this list conflicts with a previously established subject heading. In the event of a conflict between an established subject heading and a subdivision on this list, use the established heading unless a decision has been made to update or change all headings of that type. For example, use the established subject heading *Child abuse* rather than formulate a heading of the type *Children--Abuse of*. However, previously established headings of the type *Teachers, Training of* were changed to the form *Teachers--Training of*.

list.scope: Topical and form subdivisions usable on a free-floating basis under headings for classes of persons (age and sex groups; social, economic, political categories; afflicted persons; members of religions; employees and occupational groups; classes of persons formed with place/corporate subdivisions or ethnic/national qualifiers); not under social classes, ethnic groups/nationalities, or religious orders
general_notes: LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Textbooks*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.
Subdivisions from this list may be used under headings for groups of literary authors where there is no conflict with a subdivision specifically designated for use under literary authors in H 1155.2.

Determine if the use of a free-floating subdivision from this list conflicts with a previously established subject heading. In the event of a conflict between an established subject heading and a subdivision on this list, use the established heading unless a decision has been made to update or change all headings of that type. For example, use the established subject heading *Child abuse* rather than formulate a heading of the type *Children--Abuse of*. However, previously established headings of the type *Teachers, Training of* were changed to the form *Teachers--Training of*.
Cross-references printed in the list (May Subd Geog column "--") are not valid subdivisions; they are kept separately in see_references with their targets.
